goal.objective: Identify exactly one appended system-prompt instruction that could improve a coding agent's verification efficiency on multi-module Python tasks: catch correctness failures without increasing deadline misses. The intervention must be directly A/B testable against no appended instruction, specify how verification effort is prioritized, name its causal mechanism, and state concrete failure risks.

proposal.title: Risk-weighted verification budget
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, spend no more than 20% of the task deadline on the available checks ranked by expected correctness-failure reduction per second, prioritizing changed public interfaces and cross-module data flow, and stop when that budget is exhausted.
proposal.claim: Against no appended instruction, this instruction will increase task pass_rate without increasing the deadline-miss rate, while keeping median wall_time and turns within 5% of control.
proposal.mechanism: A hard time cap prevents open-ended testing, while expected failure reduction per second concentrates scarce verification on high-impact integration boundaries where multi-module defects are most likely to propagate.
assumptions: The agent can estimate remaining deadline time
Targeted checks exist for at least some changed interfaces
Cross-module boundary failures contribute materially to incorrect submissions
risks: The agent may estimate failure likelihood or check duration poorly
A fixed 20% cap may under-test unusually risky changes
Ranking overhead may consume part of the verification budget
Fast low-value checks may displace slower decisive checks

test_plan.experiment: Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to the appended instruction or no appended instruction under identical deadlines, tools, models, and seeds; score hidden tests and deadline completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment has higher pass_rate, no higher deadline-miss rate, and no more than 5% increases in median wall_time and turns.

proposal.title: Boundary-coverage verification
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing a multi-module change, run at most two time-bounded checks, choosing first the check that exercises the greatest number of changed module boundaries and then the fastest check covering any changed boundary not exercised by the first.
proposal.claim: Compared with no appended instruction, the treatment will raise hidden-test pass_rate without raising deadline misses, with median wall_time and turns no more than 5% above control.
proposal.mechanism: Prioritizing checks by changed-boundary coverage exposes interface, import, serialization, and call-contract failures that isolated module checks miss, while the two-check cap bounds verification cost.
assumptions: The agent can identify changed module boundaries
Available checks differ in boundary coverage
Two checks fit within typical remaining task time
risks: Broad boundary checks may be slow or flaky
Coverage estimates may be inaccurate
Two checks can miss failures deep inside one module
The second check may duplicate the first in practice

test_plan.experiment: Randomize matched multi-module Python tasks across treatment and no-instruction control with identical model, tools, seeds, and deadlines; evaluate hidden tests and whether each run finishes on time.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment improves pass_rate, does not increase deadline-miss rate, and keeps median wall_time and turns within 5% of control.

proposal.title: Fastest-falsifier priority
proposal.intervention: Use the remaining verification time only on checks ordered by shortest estimated time to a decisive failure, beginning with syntax/import validation of every changed module and then the smallest targeted test that crosses a changed call boundary; stop verification at 15% of the total deadline.
proposal.claim: Relative to no appended instruction, this bounded fastest-falsifier rule will improve pass_rate without increasing deadline-miss rate and with at most a 5% increase in median wall_time or turns.
proposal.mechanism: Cheap checks rapidly eliminate common catastrophic failures across all edited modules, leaving the bounded residual time for one high-signal integration check rather than low-yield broad testing.
assumptions: Syntax and import checks are cheap relative to the deadline
Many correctness failures manifest as imports or changed-boundary behavior
The agent can estimate check runtimes approximately
risks: Fast checks can have low semantic coverage
Runtime estimates can be wrong
A 15% cap may be too small for slow test environments
Prioritizing early failures may miss subtle end-to-end regressions

test_plan.experiment: On a fixed suite of matched multi-module Python tasks, randomly assign the instruction or no instruction while holding model, seed, tools, and deadline constant; record hidden-test outcome and deadline completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment yields higher pass_rate, no increase in deadline misses, and no more than 5% higher median wall_time and turns.

proposal.title: Dependency-fanout targeting
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, run exactly one available check under a timeout of 10% of the task deadline, selecting the check that covers the changed module with the largest downstream dependency fanout and breaks ties by shorter expected runtime.
proposal.claim: Compared with no appended instruction, dependency-fanout targeting will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses, median wall_time, or turns by more than 5%.
proposal.mechanism: Failures in high-fanout modules can invalidate many downstream paths, so testing the most propagated risk first maximizes expected caught failures per bounded verification run.
assumptions: The repository structure reveals approximate module dependency fanout
At least one check covers a changed high-fanout module
One bounded check can finish within 10% of the deadline
risks: Fanout is an imperfect proxy for defect probability
A low-fanout module may contain the actual severe bug
The chosen check may not exercise the changed behavior
Startup overhead may consume the timeout

test_plan.experiment: Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to treatment or no-instruction control with identical model, seed, tools, and deadline; score hidden tests, completion time, and interaction count.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment has higher pass_rate, no greater deadline-miss rate, and median wall_time and turns no more than 5% above control.

proposal.title: One adversarial boundary probe
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, spend at most 10% of the deadline executing one minimal end-to-end probe through the changed modules, prioritizing the input nearest a modified contract boundary that would most clearly distinguish correct from plausible incorrect behavior.
proposal.claim: Against no appended instruction, requiring one time-capped adversarial boundary probe will increase pass_rate without increasing deadline misses and with median wall_time and turns within 5% of control.
proposal.mechanism: A discriminating concrete example forces changed modules to compose on a risky edge case, exposing semantic contract mismatches that syntax checks and happy-path tests may not reveal.
assumptions: The agent can identify a modified contract boundary
A minimal cross-module probe can run within the cap
Boundary edge cases represent a meaningful share of hidden failures
risks: The selected example may be unrepresentative
Constructing the probe may take longer than executing it
The repository may lack an easy end-to-end entry point
One probe may create false confidence

test_plan.experiment: Randomize a benchmark of matched multi-module Python tasks between this appended instruction and no appended instruction under fixed model, seed, tools, and deadline; score hidden-test correctness and completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment improves pass_rate, does not increase deadline-miss rate, and limits median wall_time and turn increases to 5%.

proposal.title: Highest-uncertainty assumption check
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, identify the single correctness assumption about interactions among changed modules for which you have the least direct evidence, and spend no more than 12% of the deadline running the shortest check that can falsify it.
proposal.claim: Compared with no appended instruction, the highest-uncertainty assumption check will improve hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses, while keeping median wall_time and turns within 5% of control.
proposal.mechanism: Directing a bounded check at the weakest-supported cross-module assumption reduces epistemic blind spots more efficiently than repeating checks of already supported behavior.
assumptions: The agent can surface its key cross-module assumptions
Uncertainty roughly tracks failure risk
A falsifying check exists and fits the time cap
risks: Self-reported uncertainty may be poorly calibrated
The shortest falsifier may have weak coverage
The highest-risk failure may arise from an assumption the agent does not notice
Formulating the assumption may add overhead

test_plan.experiment: Assign matched multi-module Python tasks at random to the appended instruction or no-instruction control, holding model, seed, tools, and deadline fixed; evaluate hidden tests and deadline completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment pass_rate is higher, deadline-miss rate is not higher, and median wall_time and turns increase by no more than 5%.

proposal.title: Changed-line coverage subset
proposal.intervention: When test-to-code coverage information is available, spend at most 15% of the deadline running the smallest test subset that touches changed lines in every edited module, prioritizing tests that touch changed lines in multiple modules; otherwise perform no extra verification required by this instruction.
proposal.claim: Against no appended instruction, changed-line coverage selection will increase pass_rate without increasing deadline misses and will keep median wall_time and turns within 5% of control.
proposal.mechanism: Coverage-guided set selection removes tests unrelated to the patch while favoring tests that exercise interactions across edited modules, increasing relevant failure detection per unit time.
assumptions: Usable test-to-code coverage data is available on a meaningful fraction of tasks
Historical coverage predicts which tests exercise changed behavior
The selected subset fits the time cap
risks: Coverage data may be stale
Line coverage does not prove behavioral coverage
Computing or loading coverage mappings may add overhead
Tasks without coverage data receive no benefit

test_plan.experiment: Randomize matched multi-module Python tasks to treatment or no appended instruction under identical model, seed, tools, and deadline, stratifying analysis by coverage-data availability; score hidden tests and completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Overall treatment pass_rate is higher, deadline-miss rate is not higher, and median wall_time and turns remain within 5% of control.

proposal.title: Invariant differential probe
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, use at most 10% of the deadline for one differential probe comparing pre-change and post-change behavior on an input whose result should remain invariant, prioritizing an input that traverses the most edited modules.
proposal.claim: Compared with no appended instruction, one bounded invariant differential probe will improve hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses, median wall_time, or turns by more than 5%.
proposal.mechanism: A pre/post oracle detects unintended regressions without requiring the agent to derive an exact expected value, and maximizing edited-module traversal raises the chance of exposing composition errors.
assumptions: A pre-change executable state or equivalent output is available
At least one relevant behavior should remain invariant
The probe can execute within the cap
risks: The agent may choose behavior that was intended to change
The old behavior may already be incorrect
Environment nondeterminism may create false differences
Restoring or invoking the pre-change state may add overhead

test_plan.experiment: Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to the appended instruction or no instruction with identical model, seed, tools, repository state, and deadline; evaluate hidden tests and on-time completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment increases pass_rate, does not increase deadline-miss rate, and keeps median wall_time and turns no more than 5% above control.

proposal.title: Cross-module failure-path check
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, spend at most 10% of the deadline on the fastest executable check of error propagation across a changed module boundary, prioritizing the boundary with the least existing negative-path coverage.
proposal.claim: Against no appended instruction, this bounded failure-path check will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses and with no more than 5% higher median wall_time or turns.
proposal.mechanism: Multi-module implementations often pass happy paths while mishandling exceptions, sentinel values, cleanup, or retries; targeting the least-covered negative boundary adds orthogonal failure detection at bounded cost.
assumptions: At least one changed boundary has an executable failure path
Existing negative-path coverage can be estimated
The selected check fits within the time cap
risks: Failure injection may require expensive setup
The chosen error path may be irrelevant to hidden tests
Coverage estimates may be wrong
Focusing on negative paths may miss ordinary value errors

test_plan.experiment: Randomize matched multi-module Python tasks between treatment and no-instruction control while holding model, seed, tools, and deadline fixed; score hidden tests and on-time completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment improves pass_rate, does not increase deadline-miss rate, and keeps median wall_time and turns within 5% of control.

proposal.title: Semantic-diff risk targeting
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, spend no more than 12% of the deadline on one targeted check for the highest-risk diff hunk, ranking public signature or schema changes first, control-flow and exception changes second, and internal value changes third, with cross-module consumers breaking ties.
proposal.claim: Compared with no appended instruction, semantic-diff risk targeting will raise hidden-test pass_rate without raising deadline misses and with median wall_time and turns no more than 5% above control.
proposal.mechanism: A fixed, auditable risk ordering concentrates bounded verification on changes most likely to violate contracts or propagate across modules instead of treating all edited lines equally.
assumptions: Diff hunks can be classified reliably enough
The risk ordering correlates with correctness impact
A targeted check exists for the top-ranked hunk
risks: A low-ranked internal value change may contain the actual bug
Public changes may be intentional and well covered already
Classification and consumer tracing add overhead
One check may not cover multiple interacting hunks

test_plan.experiment: Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to treatment or no appended instruction with fixed model, seeds, tools, and deadlines; measure hidden-test results and completion timing.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment has higher pass_rate, no higher deadline-miss rate, and no more than 5% increases in median wall_time and turns.

proposal.title: Historical failure-yield selection
proposal.intervention: When test history is available, use at most 15% of the deadline to run impacted tests in descending order of non-flaky failure frequency divided by median runtime, stopping at the cap; exclude tests whose flake rate exceeds 5%.
proposal.claim: Against no appended instruction, historical failure-yield selection will improve pass_rate without increasing deadline misses, median wall_time, or turns by more than 5%.
proposal.mechanism: Empirical failure yield per second prioritizes tests with demonstrated defect-detection value, while impact filtering avoids unrelated tests, flake exclusion avoids wasted debugging, and the cap bounds delay.
assumptions: Per-test runtime, failure, and flake history is available
Historical failure yield transfers to current patches
Impact mapping identifies tests related to changed modules
risks: History may be sparse or stale
Rare but severe regressions may be deprioritized
A 5% flake threshold can exclude useful tests
Failure frequency may reflect old hotspots rather than current risk

test_plan.experiment: Randomize matched multi-module Python tasks with test history to treatment or no-instruction control under identical model, seed, tools, and deadline; score hidden tests and deadline completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment pass_rate is higher, deadline-miss rate is not higher, and median wall_time and turns are within 5% of control.

proposal.title: One cross-module metamorphic check
proposal.intervention: Before finalizing, spend at most 12% of the deadline on one metamorphic check whose invariant spans the greatest number of changed modules, using two minimally different inputs and stopping after the first decisive violation.
proposal.claim: Compared with no appended instruction, one bounded cross-module metamorphic check will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses and with median wall_time and turns within 5% of control.
proposal.mechanism: Metamorphic relations supply a low-cost partial oracle when exact outputs are difficult to derive, and maximizing changed-module span exposes composition errors with only two executions.
assumptions: A valid metamorphic invariant can be identified
Two executions fit the time cap
The invariant exercises meaningful changed behavior
risks: The proposed invariant may not actually hold
Two inputs provide narrow coverage
Stateful or nondeterministic behavior may produce false violations
Designing the relation may cost more than a conventional test

test_plan.experiment: Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to this appended instruction or no-instruction control with identical model, seed, tools, and deadline; evaluate hidden tests and deadline completion.
test_plan.success_condition: Treatment improves pass_rate, does not increase deadline-miss rate, and keeps median wall_time and turns no more than 5% above control.

selections.reason: It provides the most auditable prioritization rule: an explicit semantic-risk ordering, a deterministic cross-module tie-breaker, and a 12% deadline cap. The mechanism directly connects contract-propagation risk to targeted verification, while the assumptions and risks candidly cover misranking, overhead, and limited coverage. Its randomized control protocol and bounded success criteria make it straightforward to A/B test.

The intervention is unusually concrete and auditable: it fixes both a semantic risk hierarchy and a cross-module tie-break rule, then bounds execution at 12% of the deadline. That creates a clear causal link from contract-propagation risk to verification priority, exposes realistic failure modes, and supports a clean randomized A/B test without depending on historical coverage or test telemetry.

Its fixed semantic-diff ranking is more reproducible than subjective uncertainty or expected-yield estimates, and unlike history- or coverage-based options it applies without extra telemetry. The cross-module-consumer tie-break directly addresses the task setting, the 12% cap protects deadlines, and the stated risks accurately delimit when the causal proxy can fail.

This proposal best balances correctness signal and deadline protection: its explicit hunk categories and consumer-based tie-break make prioritization inspectable, its single-check 12% cap is bounded, and its mechanism focuses on contract violations that propagate across modules. The intervention is broadly applicable without requiring coverage or historical data, and the protocol states measurable comparative success and concrete proxy failures.
